payload.comment: Reporting stage is internally consistent and complete. All cross-artifact arithmetic verified: (1) abstain_rate + test_coverage = 1.0 exactly; (2) human_review_count = 7180 × 0.385794 = 2770; (3) selective_risk = 1 − accuracy_on_covered = 0.031293; (4) confusion-matrix row sums match per-class supports (total 7180), diagonal sum 6267/7180 = 0.872841 matches reported accuracy; (5) per-class precision and recall recomputed from the confusion matrix match all reported values to 6+ decimal places; (6) evaluation_report accuracy (0.872841) equals abstention_report base_test_accuracy; (7) prediction_artifact test_samples (7180) equals evaluation n_samples; (8) search_report test_metrics_used=false confirms no test leakage into model selection; (9) OOD overall AUROC (0.935893) is consistent with per-scenario test AUROCs (0.877–0.973) under a pooled-prediction computation; (10) all schema_version fields are 1.0; (11) OOD evidence path and SHA-256 are present and well-formed. No deterministic inconsistencies found. The warning-level observations carried from prior anomaly stages (validation–test coverage gap, limited OOD corruption scope, 38.6% abstention burden, class-7 recall 0.489, inert transformer config fields) are legitimate methodological caveats but do not constitute reporting errors; they are appropriately scoped as warnings and do not invalidate the reported numbers. The reporting dossier is ready for downstream consumption.
llm_issues: Validation–test coverage gap (80% val → 61.4% test) and ~40× risk gap (0.00075 vs 0.0313) mean selective-prediction guarantees are weaker on test than validation suggests; deployment planning should use test-side risk figures.
OOD evaluation is limited to additive Gaussian noise (σ ∈ {0.15, 0.25, 0.4}); ood_pass should be interpreted as a narrow corruption-robustness proxy, not a full distribution-shift guarantee.
38.6% abstention rate (2 770 samples) represents a significant human-review burden; risk-coverage curve shows diminishing returns above 70% target coverage.
Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma) test recall is 0.489 (CI95 0.442–0.537); 97 samples misclassified as debris and 57 as smooth muscle – highest-impact error pattern.
Class 0 → class 5 confusion (306/1338, 22.9%) drives class-5 precision to 0.567 – largest off-diagonal block in the confusion matrix.

Inert transformer config fields (num_heads, patch_size, pooling, positional_encoding, tokenizer_layers, mlp_ratio) persist in the resnet18 train_config; functionally harmless but create schema ambiguity for downstream tooling.
early_stopping_patience=3 is below the commonly recommended 8–12; did not trigger in this run but could cause premature stopping in a re-run with a different seed.
class_weighting disabled despite 1.63× class imbalance; minority-class recall (class 7: 0.489) suggests under-served classes.
hidden=32 channels is below the commonly recommended 64–128 range for 28×28 CNNs; empirically justified by search but is a documented deviation.
vflip augmentation may produce anatomically implausible orientations for histopathology images; low risk given strong overall metrics but a per-class sanity check is advisable.
